summary: Tested both new features on the preview URL at 375x667, plus the backend. (1) Map stop details work. On /admin/route/route-review, the expand button (44x44, bottom-right) opens route-map-fullscreen with the header 'R-REVIEW Downtown · TAP A STOP'. Tapping marker 1 shows map-stop-details '1. Alex Morgan', with the address '200 King St W, Kitchener', a PENDING pill and RV1001. Tapping marker 3 and then marker 2 switches the card (Sam Taylor, then Jamie Lee). map-stop-details-close hides the card and the fullscreen stays open. route-map-fullscreen-close closes the fullscreen. Reopening shows no leftover card, and Escape closes it. Also checked: H-1025 Stanley Park (completed) shows DELIVERED and FAILED pills and the window, e.g. 'MH2049 · 25 SUN 09:00–11:00'. R-101 Downtown (active, with driver marker) shows all 6 stops correctly. Dashboard card admin-route-R-121 → route page → stop 5 shows 'TEST API Customer … MC77155 · 17:30–20:30'. Markers on the inline (small) map are disabled, as designed. On the driver screen (Marcus, drv-1, R-101), the fullscreen opens with 'R-101 Downtown · PINCH TO ZOOM'. Markers there are aria-disabled and tapping one shows no card, as expected. No page errors. (2) Deletion confirmation works. test_account_deletion.py: 13/13 pass. The new unit tests test_deletion_confirmations.py: 6/6 pass. They check that the store email goes to each recipient with the name HTML-escaped and that email failures are caught. They also check that the driver SMS goes to real numbers and is skipped for fictional 555-01xx numbers, empty phones and missing Twilio env, and that Twilio errors are caught. The POST still returns 200 {ok:true}. During the run backend.err.log shows only email/send 202 Accepted, with no warnings or tracebacks. I fixed a test-safety problem first: the deletion tests made random +1519xxxxxxx driver phones, so with the new SMS a real stranger could have been texted. They now use fictional +151955501xx numbers.

minor.issue: db.drivers.find({}) does not filter out deleted drivers. A self-deleted driver still shows in the Admin dashboard 'DRIVER SCORECARDS' as rank 5 'Deleted driver' (seen live: drv-deltest-91225d, deleted at 16:36 by an earlier run, not mine). Other driver lists already filter with {'deleted': {'$ne': True}}.

confirm_store / confirm_driver / notify_admin are awaited inline, one after another (email timeout is 30s each). A slow email provider can delay the 200 by tens of seconds after the account is already wiped. Consider asyncio.create_task / BackgroundTasks.

issues: The selected stop is not highlighted on the map, so it's unclear which marker the card belongs to, especially when markers overlap. Example: H-1025 Stanley Park, where marker 2 is mostly covered by marker 7.

When the details card opens, the map gets shorter and is re-projected, so every marker jumps (marker 1 moved from y621 to y499). The stop just tapped moves out from under the finger. Consider overlaying the card on the map instead of resizing it.
On the web fallback, the driver marker View renders on top of the stop markers and can block taps on a stop under it (R-101: driver square next to stop 1).

action_items: Filter deleted drivers out of the scorecards query (routes/scorecards.py:141: add {'deleted': {'$ne': True}}).
Optional: send the deletion confirmation emails/SMS and the admin email in the background so a slow provider can't delay the response.
Optional UX: highlight the selected marker in fullscreen, and overlay the stop card instead of shrinking the map.
Leftover test data from an earlier run (not created by me): drv-deltest-91225d plus its merchant/user (mer-deltest-91225d). Clean up by exact id if it came from your run.
critical_code_review_comments: account.py: the driver's phone and the store recipients are read before being wiped. Correct.
account.py: confirm_store runs before the audit log and the admin email. Errors are caught, so the deletion itself can't fail because of email.

ExpandableRouteMap: onMarkerPress is passed only to the fullscreen map, and only when details are given, so the driver screen stays non-tappable. Admin labels use index+1 and the driver screen uses st.seq. Both match their own lists.
RouteMap.android.tsx: any WebView postMessage is treated as a marker id. That's safe, because details[id] just returns undefined for unknown ids.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_account_deletion.py (throwaway driver phones changed to fictional +151955501xx so the new SMS never texts a real number)
seed_data_creation: None kept. The pytest throwaway store/drivers were created and removed by exact id.
